items.title: Breath-Dx: A Time Series Classification Benchmark for Disease Screening with eNose
items.summary: Electronic nose (eNose) technology offers a portable, non-invasive route for disease screening via exhaled breath analysis. However, progress in the field is hindered by the lack of systematic benchmarks that compare machine learning methods under realistic conditions, particularly sensor drift, a known but rarely quantified failure mode. Most existing studies rely on small, private datasets with inconsistent protocols, rendering results non-comparable and slowing progress. We introduce Breath-Dx, the first comprehensive benchmark of time series classification methods for breath-based disease …

items.title: Weight-Space Programming Doesn't Need Transformers
items.summary: Standard neural architectures such as the Transformer were chosen because they train well with gradient descent and run fast on GPUs. In weight-space programming, a large language model (LLM) writes target weights by hand without gradient-based training, so those reasons no longer apply. Should we keep the Transformer? Given minimal guidance, ten labeled examples, and a sandbox, mainly on multiple-choice questions, we task three frontier LLMs with either generating the weights of a fixed architecture or designing the architecture themselves. items.title: Multi-Branch Transformer
items.summary: Transformer language models are commonly scaled by making their blocks wider or stacking them deeper. In this work, we explore a complementary path: branching, the parallel composition of full Transformer blocks. We introduce the Multi-Branch Transformer (MBT), which processes the input through shared initial layers, executes independently parameterized branches of sequential blocks in parallel, and fuses their outputs before shared final layers. At comparable training compute, we study three MBT variants: Wide-Shallow preserves block width, Narrow-Deep preserves sequential depth, and Balanced…

items.title: MedJev: A System One Vision-Language Decision Model for Fast and Effective Medical Image Understanding
items.summary: Medical image understanding with vision-language models (VLMs) typically relies on autoregressively generating reasoning and answer tokens. These unnecessary tokens make the inference cost scale with the response length and force the answer to be parsed from free-form text, incurring avoidable latency and decision errors. To this end, we introduce MedJev, a system one vision-language decision model that maps medical images, questions, and candidate answers directly to decisions in a single multimodal forward pass, without any autoregressive generation process. items.title: ForceHarness: Turning Force into Action and Physics for Frozen Frontier Models
items.summary: Frontier multimodal models can now control robots zero-shot from images, yet many manipulation tasks depend on contact forces that images cannot show. Bringing force to an API-only frozen model raises two challenges. First, contact evolves much faster than an API model can decide, so the system must close the loop on force beneath the model. Second, a frozen model cannot interpret raw force streams, so force must be returned in a form the model can reason about. items.summary: Abstention, the withholding of a response by a large language model (LLM) under uncertainty or safety risks, is essential for trustworthy models. The causes of abstention fall into three perspectives: ambiguity in the Query (Q), limits of Model Knowledge (MK), and misalignment with Human Values (HV). However, prior analyses of internal representations have focused on HV, using a refusal direction computed from harmful and harmless queries. No study has analyzed the three perspectives jointly. items.summary: We built a hybrid multi-agent trading system that combines large language model (LLM) analysts with momentum-based portfolio construction and rule-based execution. Company-news and macroeconomic agents return structured reports to a coordinator that sets stock weights and cash reserves. We evaluate the portfolio engine using its broker-recorded paper account, which operated with deterministic fallbacks, and compare LLM-enabled configurations through retrospective replays. items.summary: Fine-tuning data can include metadata that predicts the correct answer, such as a reward-model score or a quality label. We ask whether a model learns to rely on this metadata even when every training label is correct. items.title: Energy-Based Reasoners: Your Recurrent Reasoner Should Be an Energy-Based Model
items.summary: Looping is a powerful inductive bias for reasoning. By repeatedly iterating a recurrent block, looped models can scale their effective depth and enable multi-step reasoning in latent space. However, existing looped models are not inherently guided by an explicit measure of progress, making it difficult to determine when to stop looping and how to improve upon the current state. items.summary: High-resolution brain MRI is important for neuroradiological assessment, yet routine clinical protocols often rely on fast, anisotropic 2D acquisitions, particularly in resource-constrained settings. These acquisitions may differ in orientation, alignment and anatomical coverage, resulting in partially overlapping image stacks. Existing learning-based super-resolution methods typically rely on single, under-constrained inputs or fixed multi-stack configurations with idealised acquisition geometry. items.summary: Evaluations of multi-agent language models often compare communicating architectures against a single greedy pass. This practice confounds coordination with sample multiplicity and inference compute. We synthesize nine primary empirical evaluations comprising 516 unique multi-agent configurations organized along a resource vector R with six dimensions and a baseline ladder with four categories. items.summary: Speech applications require decisions about term presence, turn completion, and language within an audio window. We present Marimba, an interface for typed speech decisions built on frozen Qwen3-ASR 0.6B features. Lexical questions use zero-shot scoring of ASR transcripts; non-lexical questions use a question-conditioned head and a separate layer-18 turn-end readout. items.summary: LLM agents answer questions by calling APIs and trusting the results. An API can fail silently. It ignores part of a request, such as a misnamed filter, yet returns HTTP 200 and a plausible but wrong result. Current fixes, such as checklists, reviewer models and LLM judges, ask the model to catch it. But models often see the problem and answer anyway. We present SilentGuard, which moves the decision from the model to the harness running tool calls. items.summary: When language models revise a decision after another agent disagrees, neither reversal counts nor final accuracy shows whether they are fixing mistakes or abandoning correct answers. We introduce a controlled two-pass audit that holds the question, the evidence, and the model's initial answer fixed and varies only the revision context: neutral reflection, anonymous disagreement, or disagreement attributed to a domain expert. items.summary: Visual agents answer questions about ultra-high-resolution photos by zooming into the relevant regions. However, existing agents often answer from common sense instead of reading the evidence. Reinforcement learning (RL) on the final answer cannot correct this, because a guess earns the same reward as reading. We propose Cross-Input Relative Policy Optimization (CrossRPO), which trains agents on contrast sets. items.summary: Legal reasoning in civil-law systems is not rule-lookup: the German state examination asks for a structured opinion (Gutachten) that names the governing norms, applies them to the facts, and argues to a conclusion. We introduce GPBam (German Public Law Bar-style Exam), 81 public-law examination cases with reference solutions, paired with a recitation task over 200 statutory provisions. items.title: BitDecoding-FP4: Native FP4 KV Cache Decoding via Algorithm-System Co-Design
items.summary: The key-value (KV) cache dominates memory capacity and bandwidth in long-context LLM serving. While 4-bit microscaling formats (NVFP4, MXFP4) shrink the cache and run attention on FP4 Tensor Cores, a fundamental gap remains between algorithmic quantization and system-aware acceleration: existing FP4 KV systems use vanilla quantization that causes severe accuracy drops, whereas accuracy-oriented 4-bit algorithms rely on vector codebooks whose lookup overhead degrades decoding throughput. items.title: Termination Lag: Coding Agents Solve Early but Stop Late
items.summary: Coding agents can solve a task well before they stop working on it. We characterize termination lag--the number of steps between an agent's first correct patch and the end of its run--across five models, two agent frameworks, and three SWE-bench datasets by recording and testing every distinct repository patch generated during execution. items.title: JEPA4R: Embodied JEPA World Models with 4D Point Planning
items.summary: Joint-embedding predictive architecture (JEPA) world models predict future embeddings instead of pixels and plan in latent space. Two challenges remain: 2D images leave the metric geometry that manipulation acts on implicit and entangled with appearance, and what these models imagine stays hidden, as they are mostly judged in simulation by short-horizon latent planning. items.title: Zuse: A Decision Model for European Languages
items.summary: Decision models read a document and return a probability for each of a fixed set of options instead of generating text. Several appeared in 2026, but none has published results outside English. We describe Zuse, three decision models (4B, 9B and 27B) that train a low-rank adapter and a pointer head on frozen open-weight bases, targeting 27 European languages, and use them to study how this design behaves across languages and tasks. items.title: LynnReal-Hand: Unlocking World Interaction with Hand Control
items.summary: Interactive video world models enable exploration through text and camera controls, yet direct object interaction requires finer control. Hands provide a natural interface, but translating continuous hand movements into coherent visual responses remains challenging because of complex hand-object dynamics and demanding real-time computation. To address these challenges, we introduce LynnReal-Hand, a hand-controlled video world model that unifies precise interaction modeling with efficient streaming generation. items.summary: Robots in homes, warehouses and farms must pick up objects they have never seen, usually without a 3D model or a category label. A grasping policy that works directly on the point cloud from a depth sensor needs only the geometry the robot observes, so it applies to any new object. Offline grasp generators such as Contact-GraspNet work this way, but they rank grasps by learned plausibility rather than by whether the grasp actually lifts the object. items.title: Dataset Distillation via Drifting
items.summary: The task of dataset distillation concerns the learning of a small set of synthetic samples that can serve as an effective replacement for a large real dataset when used for downstream tasks. While many solutions have been proposed since the problem's inception, most of them primarily seek to optimize the distilled data with respect to a classifier. In this work, we propose a new distillation method that learns a set of samples such that they directly approximate the per-class data distribution. items.summary: In particle physics, discrepancies between experimental measurements and Standard Model (SM) predictions are commonly interpreted within new theoretical models. In this context, the Standard Model Effective Field Theory (SMEFT) provides a general framework encompassing a broad class of models. items.title: Fine-Grained Japanese Clinical Named Entity Recognition: A Controlled Comparison of BERT and Open-Weight Large Language Models
items.summary: Background: Generative large language models (LLMs) offer an alternative to encoder-based clinical named entity recognition (NER), but their performance on fine-grained Japanese extraction tasks and sensitivity to generation settings remain uncertain. Methods: We compared two fine-tuned BERT-CRF baselines with nine open-weight LLMs on iCorpus, which defines 113 entity categories. items.summary: Optimal Transport (OT) provides a principled framework for finding the minimum cost coupling between probability distributions. Classical solvers remain the gold standard for this task. At the same time, OT is an ideal testbed for studying whether learning-based amortized models can internalize the structure of OT type problems. items.title: Communicate the Change: Efficient Expert Parallelism via Activation Compression
items.summary: Scaling has driven the success of large language models (LLM), with sparse mixture-of-experts (MoE) architectures enabling greater parameter capacity without a proportional increase in computation. At large scales, MoE models rely on expert parallelism to distribute experts across devices. items.title: Joint-ID: Transformer-based Joint Image Enhancement and Depth Estimation for Underwater Environments
items.summary: Underwater imaging is a challenging task due to factors such as scattering, absorption, and turbulence, which degrade image quality and limit visibility. In this paper, we propose a novel approach for enhancing underwater images that leverages the benefits of joint learning for simultaneous image enhancement and depth estimation. We introduce Joint-ID, a transformer-based neural network that can obtain high-perceptual image quality and depth information from raw underwater images. items.summary: Preference alignment has become a central tool to align large language models (LLMs) with human values and desired behavior, and its online variant can further advance their capabilities beyond what static data alone offer by repeatedly generating and labeling new responses with human feedback. items.summary: Reconstructing animatable 3D human avatars from images is important for applications such as gaming and augmented reality. Feedforward methods make avatar reconstruction accessible by reducing inference time to a few seconds, but recent approaches rely heavily on scaling model capacity, training data, and computation. items.summary: This study proposes a Cucker-Smale model incorporating dynamic networks and the discrete $p$-Laplacian ($p \in (1,2)$) and analyzes the relationship between flocking time constraints and graph connectivity from both theoretical and experimental perspectives. items.summary: Large Language Models (LLMs) offer strong potential for personalized education, but adolescent-facing deployment raises risks of toxic, biased, misleading, or developmentally inappropriate content. We argue that educational safety should move beyond binary refusal: student queries are often ambiguous or curiosity-driven, requiring contextual guidance rather than simple blocking. items.summary: Noise-unconditioned denoising learns a single score, so generation can be viewed as gradient ascent on a fixed log-density landscape. items.title: 智算接棒：物理AI的下一个风口，在于计算基础设施

items.title: 看到老黄因为出轨被撸，我也说个自己最近的经历
items.summary: 我也说不清算不算出轨。 男开发+女测试，平时就工作上有些接触，下班后有可能一起去地铁站，从没直接联系过。 她是那种老实人牛马外包，闲聊时说她周末几乎不出门，在家里里刷剧什么的。 转折点在一次下班，我们都走晚了，吐槽老板答应她转正但食言了。说着突然就红了眼眶，情绪比较激动，我跟着安慰几句然后轻轻抱了她一下，当时走到地铁站但不同方向，地铁了就分别上车了。 后面明显感觉她对我走得近了很多。各种细节也不好一一列举，比如讨论问题时候的距离比之前近了，但还是正常距离。我能感觉到变化但谁也没说破。我自己有家庭，即使有想法也承担不起这个风险。过一俩星期感觉又恢复到之前了。 我有个老家亲戚，平时不联系，我妈在月初跟我打电话说他在跑外卖出事故住院了，让我去看看，我定了上周末自己开车去，在上海青浦。然后下班跟她聊天说到这个事了，结果她来了一句“xhs 上淀山湖 blabla，想去看看”，问我放不方便带上她。虽然我大概知道是啥意思，但还是答应了。当天来回，湖边找个露营地聊了聊人生，拉了拉手。后面送她到小区门口，我没下车，没有临门一脚。路上问她怎么吃饭，她问我想吃啥请我吃，我说不用了，老婆在家做好了。 以上真实经历，讲出来，就是想说，我也不是什么高尚的人，这种事情也是人之常情，我老婆不查岗也不翻我隐私，我没做得过多只是风险和后果对我影响太大，有房贷有小孩。如果风险足够低，比如她不是我办公室的同事，或者我没有…

items.title: 黑苹果 x86 最后的容光了
items.summary: 最近两天把原本 13.7.8 的黑苹果系统升级到 15.8.7，所有外设全部能用。 苹果说 26 才是最后一代支持 x86 的系统，虽然硬件也能装，可 26 删了 AppleHDA，驱动声卡只能换 VoodooHDA，但声音质量差了很多。然后 12 代的 CPU 也会有性能问题，要重测应用。只能等后面有没有驱动的更新了。 目前我使用的是 PCIe 的 Fenvi T919 扩展卡，机身上的 Intel Wi-Fi/蓝牙的功能直接关闭，这样就是纯博通的方案，苹果原生的 AirDrop / Sidecar / Apple Watch 解锁 就都能用了。代价就是必须打 OCLP root patch 补丁，而且后续如果有小版本更新，要重新打补丁。不过我打算这套系统养老了，不再更新 以上 我这套全原生驱动的 15.8.7 应该还能再战一年半载，吧。 https://i.imgur.com/ohlyutH.png https://i.imgur.com/IJYRwis.png

items.summary: ## 先说结论 中国电信光猫里预装了一个叫 `m01-b01-inner` 的插件（由 `b01odmv3` 启动），很多人在 `ps` 里见过它，但它真正的业务代码是加密的 Lua 脚本，加载后不落盘，所以过去几年网上的讨论都停留在"疑似上报 MAC"。 我从两台电信光猫的进程内存里把解密后的 Lua 源码完整导了出来，逐个模块读了一遍。结论： 1. **默认就开着**的一个模块（`xid`），写明用途是 "Collect user identification information from HTTP"，从你经过光猫的 HTTP 流量的网址、Referer、Cookie 里匹配**手机号、IMEI、IMSI、MEID、OAID、AndroidID、IDFA、IDFV、经纬度、设备型号**，每 30 分钟上报一次。 2. 插件具备**远程以 root 执行任意命令并回传结果**的能力（`shell` 模块）。 3. 插件具备**从电信服务器下载扫描程序、扫描你家整个局域网端口和服务**的能力（`pscan` 模块，参数与 nmap 一致）。 4. 插件能记录 HTTP 完整网址、User-Agent、Cookie，HTTPS 访问的域名，DNS 查询，连接五元组，甚至**原始数据包**；能**劫持重定向**你访问的网页；能**远程替换自身代码**。 5. 第 2～4 条的大部分…

items.title: AI 切碎了我的注意力
items.summary: ## 分享一个我现在的工作感受 我经常在做任务 A 的时候，接受到 B 的信息，然后脑子会迅速切到 B，然后执行一会 B 再被 C 吸引，执行一会 C。然后再回到 A。我自己比喻自己像个 cpu，多线程在不同的任务上分配注意力。 我自己感觉是大脑经常保持高敏感状态，怕错过信息，所以很容易捕捉周围的信息，一发现有可能有价值的，就忍不住马上投入。这样的好处是，信息收集比较强，容易捕捉新的东西。缺点就是长任务难执行，容易半途而废。
